papers.title: TileDRAM: Compiler-Controlled Tile-to-DRAM Layouts for 3D DRAM GPGPUs
authors: Guangyuan Xu, Lanxuan Zhang, Ziyang Li, Zhaoshi Li, Yajun Ha
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2610.23767v1 Announce Type: new

papers.title: MemLLM: End-to-end In-Storage Acceleration of On-device Retrieval-Augmented Generation using Precomputed KV Caches
authors: Seungkwan Kang, Hyungseok Ko, Heemin Kim, Myoungsoo Jung
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2610.22579v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) on edge devices enables personalized large language model (LLM) inference while preserving privacy. However, RAG's inherent length asymmetry makes the prefill phase the dominant bottleneck. While precomputing the KV caches offline alleviates the prefill cost on server systems, the multi-gigabyte caches over the narrow interconnect create a severe I/O wall for on-device systems. To mitigate this, we propose MemLLM, an end-to-end in-storage processing (ISP) architecture that executes the complete attention pipeline based on precomputed KV caches within the SSD. papers.title: HBFSim: A Simulator for Exploring HBF in Memory Hierarchies for LLMs
authors: Jinheng Li, Guosheng Wang, Hongchao Du, Shangyu Wu, Qiao Li, Chun Jason Xue
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2610.23503v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) has recently emerged as a promising technology that provides terabyte-scale accelerator-local capacity at bandwidths approaching HBM, with a potential cost-per-bit advantage over HBM. However, its NAND foundation brings long latency, out-of-place updates, and finite write endurance directly into the accelerator memory hierarchy, making its effects on performance and lifetime difficult to predict. To study this emerging design space, we present HBFSim, an LLM-aware event-driven simulator for heterogeneous HBM+HBF memory systems that preserves application-level memory semantics while modeling flash-internal behavior. papers.title: Rethinking Agentic Kernel Generation for Emerging Accelerators
authors: Ruijie Gao, Jirong Yang, Barry Lyu, Haoran Jin, Nathan Bleier
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2608.00894v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Emerging accelerators often lack mature compiler backends, motivating neural agents that generate and repair kernels from architectural documentation and simulator feedback. This approach repeatedly reconstructs workload-invariant machine semantics, including instruction behavior, legality constraints, synchronization rules, and memory protocols, for every workload. We argue that these semantics should be compiled once into a persistent symbolic artifact, while neural reasoning should focus on workload-dependent mapping decisions.
